Thanks Aditya — locking this in from a scope and scoring perspective. A few notes from the hiring manager side to align the panel before invites go out.

Role scope (short):
- This is a Staff-level role focused on production LLM inference: building runtime features that reduce tail latency, manage KV cache behavior, and enable efficient batching across multi-tenant workloads. Ownership includes the serving runtime, performance tooling, and cross-team rollout of caching/quantization defaults.

Leveling expectations (what distinguishes Staff from Senior):
- Technical depth: Staff should demonstrate low-level optimization experience (profiling, kernel tradeoffs) and make principled choices about quantization and batching. Senior may know the techniques; Staff must design reliable, repeatable patterns for a product team.
- Scope and influence: Staff drives cross-team design and owns a production surface (latency/SLOs, cost budgets). Look for evidence of shipped systems with measurable unit-economics improvements.
- Ambiguity & tradeoffs: Staff handles ambiguous specs (e.g., balancing throughput vs. tail latency under high cardinality) and can explain tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders.

Interview focus areas and example prompts (please keep to these during questioning and scoring):
1) Systems & architecture (30m — Karthik)
   - Evaluate end-to-end design for a multi-tenant inference service that serves both short-chat and long-context workloads. Ask candidate to reason about prefix caching and cold-start behavior.
   - Look for concrete design choices (cache invalidation, shard placement, per-tenant QoS).
2) Inference/runtime tradeoffs (25m — Naomi)
   - Deep-dive into latency optimizations: memory layout, KV cache locality, attention-kernel selection, and quantization impacts.
   - Practical prompt: we have a 4x cost gap between two approaches; ask candidate to propose measurement plans and incremental rollout steps.
3) Product & prioritization (25m — Marissa)
   - Candidate should demonstrate prioritization under resource constraints: when to invest in model-level optimizations vs serving-layer investments.
   - Ask for a roadmap pivot where 30% of requests are experiencing  p95 spikes.
4) Bar-raiser calibration (20m — Jonas)
   - Focus on culture fit, long-term ownership, and system-level thinking. Bring up a past failure and ask how they’d instrument and learn from it.

Scoring guidance (high level):
- Use 1–5 scale; 4+ expected for hire.
- Evidence required for 4: shipped production changes with quantified impact, cross-team leadership, clear tradeoff reasoning.
- For ambiguous answers, request a measurement plan or follow-up test.

Attachments: naomi_scope_notes.md (short bullets above)

One operational ask: please block a 30m debrief slot for the panel the day after the on-site (ideally 3/4). I recommend a short calibration docat the top of the invite with the scoring rubric.

I can take the inference/runtime slot; Jonas, if you can do bar-raiser that would be helpful.

Naomi

Thanks Naomi — this is great. A couple of quick thoughts from the bar-raiser perspective:

- Please emphasize the difference between tactical micro-optimizations and system-level ownership. I will probe for examples where the candidate made a tradeoff that improved business-level metrics (latency or cost) and how they validated it.
- For the inference/runtime prompt: add a small follow-up where the candidate proposes an A/B plan that can be rolled out to 10% of traffic with rollback criteria defined. That helps separate good intuition from actionable engineering.
- Scoring nuance: if someone has strong technical depth but limited cross-team shipping experience, rate them a 3 and flag for a follow-up engineering-lead hire conversation.

I can take the bar-raiser slot on Wed 3/3 12:00 PT if needed.

Jonas
